lessons.title: Lesson 1: Ratios & Unit Rates in Real-World Contexts
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Intro to Ratios & Solving Unit Rate Problems
lessons.reading: A ratio compares two quantities. A rate compares two quantities with different units (such as miles and hours, or dollars and items). A unit rate has a denominator of 1 unit (for example, $6 per pound or 55 miles per 1 hour) and is found by dividing the first quantity by the second.

principles.title: Computing Unit Rates by Division
principles.summary: Divide total cost or distance by quantity to find the rate per 1 unit.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Finding a Percent of a Quantity
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Percents as Ratios Per 100
lessons.reading: Percent means "per hundred" (p% = p/100). To find p% of a number, convert the percentage to a decimal by dividing by 100 (or write it as a fraction over 100) and multiply by the whole quantity.

principles.title: Calculating Percent of a Number
principles.summary: Express p% as p/100 and multiply by the base quantity.

units.title: Unit 2: Fraction Division, Integers & Algebraic Equations

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Dividing Fractions & Operating with Negative Integers
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Dividing Fractions by Fractions & Negative Numbers
lessons.reading: To divide a fraction by another fraction, multiply the dividend by the reciprocal (multiplicative inverse) of the divisor: (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b) × (d/c), then simplify using the greatest common divisor. On the number line, negative integers lie to the left of 0; adding a positive integer moves right, while subtracting moves left.

principles.title: Dividing Fractions by Multiplying by the Reciprocal
principles.summary: Invert the second fraction (divisor) and multiply numerators and denominators, then simplify.

principles.title: Adding & Subtracting Signed Integers
principles.summary: Use number-line direction and absolute value to evaluate signed integer expressions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Evaluating Expressions with Exponents & Solving Linear Equations
lessons.reading: When evaluating an algebraic expression like 4x² - 7 for a given value of x, substitute the number for x and follow the Order of Operations (PEMDAS: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication/Division, Addition/Subtraction). To solve an equation such as mx + b = c, apply inverse operations to both sides to isolate x.

principles.title: Evaluating Expressions with Exponents
principles.summary: Substitute variable values and compute exponents before multiplication and subtraction.

principles.title: Solving Equations Using Inverse Operations
principles.summary: Undo addition/subtraction first, then divide by the coefficient of x.

units.title: Unit 3: Geometry (Triangles & Prisms) and Data Statistics

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Area of Triangles, Volume of Prisms & Mean/Median
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Area of Triangles, Volume & Mean/Median
lessons.reading: Every triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height, so Area = ½ × b × h. The volume of a rectangular prism is Volume = length × width × height (cubic units). In statistics, the mean is the arithmetic average (sum of values divided by count) and the median is the middle value when data are ordered from least to greatest.

principles.title: Area of Triangles and Volume of Rectangular Prisms
principles.summary: Use A = ½bh for triangles and V = lwh for rectangular prisms.

principles.title: Measures of Center: Mean and Median
principles.summary: Compute the mean (sum ÷ count) and median (middle value of ordered list).
